scope.mode: Read-only static review. No source edits, build, emulator, or publication.
checks: All five files decode with strict UTF-8 (throwOnInvalidBytes=true); no U+FFFD replacement characters.
Both string resource files parse as XML and contain 203 unique string names, with no missing or duplicate translations.
All five formatted resources have identical indexed placeholder signatures across locales: speed_value, transfer_amount, file_size_value, delete_confirmation, timeline_task.
Neither locale defines plurals; no dynamic quantity resource requiring Arabic plural forms was found in the scoped files.
Error resource pairs retain matching error conditions and recovery guidance. PipelineException maps to resource IDs.
NeonTheme contains no hardcoded user-facing messages; fixed BACK geometry is currently unused by callers, so no active RTL defect is asserted.

findings.title: Remove proven foreign Unicode characters from the Arabic RC5 review paragraph

evidence.codepoint: U+0261 LATIN SMALL LETTER SCRIPT G
U+0261 LATIN SMALL LETTER SCRIPT G
U+02A1 LATIN LETTER GLOTTAL STOP WITH STROKE

findings.description: The baseline Arabic RC5 summary contains three literal IPA/Latin characters inside Arabic words or at clause boundaries. This is confirmed from decoded code points, not inferred from terminal rendering. The file remains valid UTF-8; the defect is corrupted text content, which breaks the Arabic wording of the evidence summary.
findings.recommendation: Correct the three affected Arabic fragments in line 39 and add a content check for unexpected IPA characters in Arabic documentation.

test_gaps.description: verifyTranslations checks duplicate string keys and key-set parity only. It does not compare formatting arguments, validate future plurals quantities, or catch corrupted Unicode content; current static placeholder checks pass.

Arabic/English font fallback, mixed-direction filenames and large-font clipping were not validated at runtime because builds and emulator runs were excluded from this review. Static theme review alone cannot establish those visual outcomes.
